oblique.verdict: Visually liked and viable as an alternate or future store Turret skin candidate. Retain the result. It is not an exact drop-in default and is not animation-ready: dorsal identity drift remains and the audit found 206 unnamed shells.

top.motivation: Controlled fidelity trial using the owner-preferred approved inferred-3D top shot after B1 drifted in dorsal identity.
top.verdict: Visually strong fourfold result and closer default-family dorsal read than B1. Retain it. Meshy returned the cross on the X/Z plane; the deterministic B2 orientation recipe changes only the mesh-node matrix, preserves binary geometry, UVs, materials, and PBR, and restores +Z-up fixed views.

request.texture_prompt: Restrained stylized PBR whole radial emplacement: matte graphite-navy hard-surface armor, weathered bronze cardinal plates, crisp panel seams, dark gunmetal locks and restrained wear. Preserve exactly four equal bounded cyan cardinal inlays; keep the cyan reactor as separate class energy. No extra cyan, glow spill, text, logos, labels, decals, baked shadows, floor lighting, added markings, or glossy toy plastic.

firstGate.expansionBasis: The owner explicitly liked B1, asked whether the T2 result can be animated, requested a consistent flow for the model family, and had already approved the inferred-3D top input. B2 is authorized only to test input-view fidelity; the third call remains reserved.
firstGate.reviewVerdict: B1 is visually liked and retained as an alternate/future store Turret skin candidate. B2 used the approved top view and improved the dorsal/default-family read. A deterministic B1 semantic-grouping pass subsequently proved that its loose components can be converted into rigid named groups and real clips without changing the provider surface.

b2Orientation.operation: -90 degrees around +X as the sole mesh-node matrix
remainingGates: runtime team-color and native replay review

stages.concept: Owner-approved Aegis Tortoise Turret concept, clean views, and exact top-form authority.
stages.provider: No new provider call; use the current static direct result as the runtime baseline.
stages.blender: Retain the current deterministic static-direct processing and recorded source.
stages.runtime: Mount as the whole Turret once, using the current class-model renderer contract.
stages.review: Capture identical top, side, oblique, and gameplay-camera frames.
stages.validation: Record silhouette, side profile, PBR, team-accent isolation, GLB, scale, anchors, and frame-budget evidence.
stages.decisionGate: Baseline only; retain until a candidate wins the full runtime comparison.

stages.concept: Use the approved clean-v1 four-view Turret package and exact top-form authority.
stages.provider: Reuse Standard Multi-Image task 019fb232-6e09-787f-85cc-dbaea29fb9b6 and its original exact texture prompt; no new call.
stages.blender: Apply deterministic axis, scale, origin, naming, semantic team-accent isolation, and conservative cleanup without identity redesign.
stages.runtime: Load on demand in the same whole-Turret mount and camera used by the control.
stages.review: Compare control and A from top, side, oblique, and actual gameplay distance, including neutral/red/blue team states.
stages.validation: Record identity, native parts/segmentation, topology, UV/PBR, accent masks, anchors, conformance, bytes, and frame cost.
stages.decisionGate: Serve as the provider-model-mode comparison for candidate B.

paths.name: T2 Smart Topology controlled input-view trials

stages.concept: B1 uses the pinned owner-approved clean-v1 front-three-quarter PNG; B2 uses the pinned owner-approved inferred-3D top PNG. No other input changes.
stages.provider: Run each named trial at most once with fixed Meshy T2 Smart Topology at 15,000 target polygons, the Standard Multi-Image texture prompt byte-for-byte, textured PBR 4K, and GLB output.
stages.blender: Apply the same deterministic normalization as A first; inspect native parts and segmentation before any rebuild.
stages.runtime: Load on demand in the same whole-Turret mount, camera, lighting, and scale envelope as control and A.
stages.review: Compare control, A, B1 oblique, and B2 top at matched top, side, oblique, and gameplay frames with neutral/red/blue team states. B1 remains a liked retained alternate even if B2 becomes the default-fidelity candidate.
stages.validation: Test identity preservation, native parts/segmentation, true depth, topology, UV/PBR maps, accent masks, pivots, anchors, recoil clearance, GLB conformance, bytes, and frame cost.
stages.decisionGate: B1 used one call/15 credits. B2 remains blocked until the B1 verdict is recorded and expansion is explicitly authorized; duplicate trial calls are forbidden.

paths.name: Winning provider result plus Blender functional retopology

stages.concept: Use the approved concept and exact top-form authority.
stages.provider: Use the reviewed production winner of A, B1, or B2 only as shape, normal, UV, and material evidence.
stages.blender: Rebuild clean animation-ready hub, cardinal arms, locks, team inlays, and class-energy parts while projecting only reviewed detail.
stages.runtime: Export separated deterministic modules with explicit pivots, deployment behavior, and fire/recoil anchors.
stages.review: Review identity before animation, then recoil, deployment, team glow, and projectile-origin motion in game.
stages.validation: Require manifold topology, stable normals/tangents, semantic materials, no cover clipping, valid anchors, bounded bytes, and matched captures.
stages.decisionGate: Proceed only when A, B1, or B2 has strong identity/materials but inadequate functional topology.

stages.concept: Treat the approved 3D concept, clean views, and SVG silhouette as immutable design authorities.
stages.provider: No paid provider call; provider models may be viewed only as non-authoritative reference.
stages.blender: Build true-depth hard-surface geometry, UVs, PBR materials, semantic accents, pivots, anchors, and animations deterministically.
stages.runtime: Export through the same normalized GLB and on-demand loading contract.
stages.review: Compare form fidelity and material richness against provider-led candidates in identical frames.
stages.validation: Require reproducible source, clean topology, exact silhouette tolerances, animation clearance, semantic materials, and runtime budgets.
stages.decisionGate: Prefer when deterministic editability and functional correctness outweigh provider-detail gains.

stages.concept: Package the approved concept, clean views, SVG authority, and all accepted/rejected comparison evidence.
stages.provider: Use accepted provider output only as optional reference or texture donor, never as unreviewed authority.
stages.blender: A technical artist creates the production topology, UV/PBR treatment, semantic team accents, pivots, anchors, and animation source.
stages.runtime: Integrate with the same renderer contract, scale envelope, camera, and load-on-demand policy.
stages.review: Run owner review at concept, graybox, textured, animation, and in-game gates.
stages.validation: Run the complete deterministic geometry, visual, animation, collision, conformance, byte, and performance gauntlet.
stages.decisionGate: Escalate when automated paths cannot jointly achieve identity, topology, materials, and runtime behavior.

rejectedPaths.name: Meshy Auto Split
rejectedPaths.reason: Automatic semantic part boundaries are not reliable enough for the Turret's exact hub, four arms, locks, team inlays, pivots, and recoil contract.

rejectedPaths.name: Meshy vehicle auto-rig
rejectedPaths.reason: A generic vehicle rig does not describe the radial deployment, recoil, fire-anchor, planted-lock, and whole-object mount behavior required by this asset.
